summary: The author examines NVIDIA's recent fiscal results and Anthropic's SEC filings to determine if stellar AI chip demand can jumpstart a broader market rally before Christmas. NVIDIA reports revenue of $115.8 billion - up over 100% year-over-year - with operating margins near 67%, easily beating analyst expectations. Meanwhile, Anthropic's registration statement reveals massive prior-year operating losses alongside soaring commitments for compute infrastructure and supply agreements. The speaker evaluates whether these valuations reflect genuine underlying demand or a supply-chain bubble, warning investors to scrutinize cash conversion cycles, accounts receivable, and customer concentration risks.
digest_it: Analisi approfondita dei conti record di NVIDIA e della S-1 di Anthropic per capire se l'intelligenza artificiale possa far ripartire i mercati. Vengono esaminati margini operativi, impegni di spesa pluriennali e rischi di concentrazione della clientela.
tone_evidence: The author urges vigilance regarding customer concentration, cash conversion rates, and the sustainability of massive infrastructure commitments.

key_points.point: NVIDIA posted fiscal Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, more than doubling year-over-year and beating estimates by nearly $7 billion.
NVIDIA's operating income reached $77.5 billion, representing an operating margin of nearly 67%.
NVIDIA trades at around 10.8 times forward expected earnings, roughly one-third of AMD's multiple.
Anthropic's S-1 filing shows operating losses of $104 billion over nine months, driven by massive investments and restructuring.
Anthropic's future commitments for supply, capacity, and leases total nearly $518 billion.

moments.claim: NVIDIA shattered revenue and profit expectations in its latest quarter.
moments.details: Revenue reached $115.8 billion, surging over 20% sequentially and more than 100% year-over-year. Operating income stood at $77.5 billion, giving the company an operating margin of nearly 67%.
moments.surprise: Revenues more than doubled in just one year while operating margins approached 67%.

moments.claim: NVIDIA trades at a remarkably low multiple relative to competitors.
moments.details: NVIDIA currently trades at roughly 10.8 times forward expected earnings over the next twelve months, which is about one-third of AMD's valuation multiple. Free cash flow for the quarter reached $48.4 billion.
moments.surprise: NVIDIA trades at only one-third of AMD's multiple despite record-breaking growth.

moments.claim: NVIDIA has locked in massive long-term supply and capacity commitments.
moments.details: Future commitments by fiscal year 2026 and beyond total nearly $518 billion, including $390 billion in supply and capacity, and $118 billion in maximum guarantees - such as a 20-year data center lease in Ohio with Open AI.
moments.surprise: Total infrastructure and supply commitments surpass half a trillion dollars.

moments.claim: Accounts receivable and inventories have expanded significantly.
moments.details: Accounts receivable reached $81 billion, while inventories climbed to nearly $40 billion, indicating extended payment terms for large clients and growing raw material stockpiles.
moments.surprise: Accounts receivable jumped to $81 billion as the company offers extended payment terms.

moments.claim: Anthropic's S-1 filing reveals heavy operating losses and slowing growth rates.
moments.details: Anthropic reported a net loss of $104 billion over the first nine months of the year, with operating expenses rising sharply. The second-quarter sequential growth rate showed significant slowing compared to previous quarters.
moments.surprise: Anthropic posted a nine-month operating loss exceeding $100 billion.

moments.claim: Anthropic faces substantial near-term cash outflows for infrastructure.
moments.details: Anthropic has already signed $900 billion in cumulative future cost commitments, including $70 billion due over the next twelve months, largely driven by compute hardware purchases.
moments.surprise: Anthropic's signed cost commitments reach nearly $900 billion.

predictions: NVIDIA fiscal year revenue is projected to grow by approximately 75% to around $741 billion.
catalysts: Anthropic IPO expected in coming days with pricing set before market quotation.
rumors: Investigations regarding former executives and potential export restrictions involving Asian markets.
curiosities: NVIDIA's operating margin means that out of every $100 entering the company, $67 remains after production, R&D, and overhead.
title: NVDA e Anthropic faranno ripartire il Mercato: 5 numeri da guardare prima di comprare
author: Marco Casario EXTRA
